## GET /admin-api/oid4vci-settings

`getOid4vciSettings`

**The credential issuer's own settings**

The `oid4vci.*` settings, among them the wallet an offer sends a holder to, the authorization server the credential endpoint will take a token from, the batch size, the deferred issuance timings, the offer username, whether a credential request must be encrypted, and the two that decide whether the SD-JWT VC and `ldp_vc` issuers name themselves by `did:web` or by URL.

Those two are restart-only and they change what a VERIFIER has to resolve — a key fetched from a DID document rather than from JWKS. What a credential CONTAINS is `GET /credential-claims`.

THERE IS NO POST BESIDE THIS ONE and that is not a gap: every form on the console page this mirrors posts `set-many` to /admin/config, so `POST /admin-api/config/set-many` is already the operation for it. One store, one action, two doors.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/vc` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: What the page says, and the settings it draws — described rows carrying each value's source and whether it can be changed while the service runs.

## GET /admin-api/oid4vci/last-request

`getLastCredentialRequest`

**How the OpenID4VCI issuer's last Credential Request arrived**

The media type the last Credential Request in this realm arrived with, and for an encrypted one (OpenID4VCI 1.0 section 10) the `kid`, `alg` and `enc` of its JWE — never the request itself. `seen: false` before any. A wallet cannot prove it encrypted: with `encryption_required` false the issuer accepts the plaintext and issues, so only the issuer knows what arrived. Until #594 the non-spec `/oid4vci/last_request`.

**Mirrors** `no console page — a wallet under test asks it` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**200**: The record.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alg` | string, or null |  |  |
| `at` | string |  |  |
| `contentType` | string, or null |  |  |
| `enc` | string, or null |  |  |
| `encrypted` | boolean |  |  |
| `kid` | string, or null |  |  |
| `path` | string |  |  |
| `seen` | boolean | yes |  |

## GET /admin-api/oid4vci/notifications

`getCredentialNotification`

**What a wallet told the OpenID4VCI issuer about one credential**

The record the Notification Endpoint (OpenID4VCI 1.0 section 11) keeps for the `notification_id` a Credential Response carried: `event` (`credential_accepted`, `credential_failure` or `credential_deleted`; null until the wallet notifies), `event_description` and `notified_at`. An id this issuer did not issue, or one expired, is 404 (STS-VC-0024). Until #594 the non-spec `/oid4vci/notification/:id`.

**Mirrors** `no console page — a wallet under test asks it` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:read`.

**Parameters**

| Name | In | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | query | string | yes | The `notification_id`. |

**200**: The notification record.
